## In Flight — Team Runtime Wave (ACf lanes)

- **⭐ ADR-052 PHASE 1 IS COMPLETE — all five memory items merged (SPRINT Steps 1–5).** Scratchpad + headline · the shared-digest re-key (`thread_digests`) · full-thread-load + per-agent wake serialization · **membership verbs** (`e3594cd`, 2026-08-10 — only agents *in* a thread wake on it; this is the ~70% wake-economics lever) · **the dormancy memory-write** (`311a08c`, 2026-08-11 — a thread can now END without vanishing: it moves `live → closing` with its digest still composing, every ever-member is woken once more to write **its own** closing memory, and only when all have done so does it go `dormant`). Also merged: **Step 30** (`787c675`) — an agent in ~370+ rooms **did not wake at all, every time**, because its room-id list overflowed the request URL (HTTP 414); that is exactly the shape 8 agents in many rooms creates. `main` = `056ea86`; **442 tests, typecheck strict-green; NOTHING DEPLOYED, and the runtime still wakes nobody.**
- 🔴 **Gate G1 — migrations 015, 016, 017 and 018 are written and APPLIED NOWHERE; all four must be applied IN ORDER before any deploy.** The L9 boot guard refuses to boot until they land, so it is self-enforcing rather than a step someone must remember. Applying them is Justin's call. **Gate G3** (Lucas's 8 supervised paces, 4/8 done) sits behind G1 **and** behind **SPRINT Step 24**: the mains' model pin is still `claude-opus-4-8`, Justin approved `claude-opus-5` on 2026-08-10, and his standing rule is that **we never switch a model without testing for behavior change** — the paces *are* that observation, so the pin must land first or they only prove the outgoing model. G2 and G4 are satisfied.
- **🔴 The top open item is SPRINT Step 43** — the dormancy sweep's cadence gate (the timer that stops it re-running constantly) has **no guard on its wiring**: delete the gate and all 442 tests still pass. It matters because a closing-memory write that fails at the model stage records nothing *by design* (a missing record is how the retry works), so that gate is the only thing standing between such a failure and **one ~64,000-token Opus wake every fifteen seconds** — the same runaway shape as the earlier `L7` bug. **A Phase-1 fast-follow (Steps 43, 44, 45, 7) runs BEFORE Phase 2** (Justin, 2026-08-11): consolidation built on a dormancy mechanism that can silently stop, or spend in a loop, is built on sand.
- **Open architecture question, and the biggest one in this lane: the agents have NO session.** Verified at source — every wake is a brand-new conversation with the model, so an agent's *reasoning and tool work* from the previous wake are gone; only the thread transcript and whatever it deliberately wrote down survive. Whether to adopt SDK sessions (which would reverse ADR-052 §3.2) or close the pain more cheaply through the per-thread scratchpad that already exists is unresolved, and gets its own dedicated sub-AC. Analysis, with all nine of Justin's runtime questions answered against the code: `docs/working/2026.08.11-acfm-acf-runtime-questions.md`.
- **🔴 A security class found here is UNRESOLVED PRODUCT-SIDE.** The team-runtime test suite could **execute an unvetted package downloaded from the public registry**: two guards spawned `npx tsc`, and with no local binary resolvable, npx fetched and ran a **squatted package named `tsc`**. Fixed in `evryn-team-runtime`, and written into DC's manual as the standing **SEALED-EXEC** order (never resolve an executable from the network at run time). ⚠️ **`evryn-backend`'s status is UNKNOWN, not clear** — a grep came back empty but cannot see the array-argument form (`spawnSync('npx', [...])`), so it is not a clearance. Sweep lane brief written, not yet spun: `docs/working/2026.08.11-acf-sealedexec-sweep-lane-brief.md`.

That file is composer **layer 1**, so any edit to it invalidates every agent's cached prompt prefix fleet-wide — which is why its edits batch.
